named_events.loss_description: Direct exposure to the Covid-19 pandemic is not believed to be material as the portfolio is in run-off. The underlying insurance policies were originally unwritten between 1992 and 2018, and coverage ceased before the start of the pandemic, with few exceptions. However, the secondary effects of the pandemic could still affect future claim settlements; for example, the economic fallout could lead to higher inflation and higher claims awards as a consequence.

gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced an overall gross prior year reserve strengthening of GBP 11.37 million, representing 8.50% of its opening gross claims outstanding. This development is primarily attributed to the reassessment of net claims incurred for previous accident years, which resulted in both surpluses and deficits across different lines of business. Specifically, the 2019, 2016, and 2015 years of account showed strengthening, while the 2017 year of account experienced a release. The majority of this movement is inferred to be related to the Reinsurance - Casualty line of business, which constitutes the syndicate's dominant underwriting activity.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2020 were GBP 133.8m. During 2020 the Syndicate recorded net favourable prior-year development of GBP 3.5m (surpluses of GBP 1.0m on direct business and GBP 2.5m on reinsurance accepted business) arising from reassessment of prior accident years. Offsetting this favourable development, the year included several significant transactional moves that materially increased gross reserves: a 90% ADC on S1458 increased gross and net technical provisions by GBP 82.2m, an RITC from Syndicate 3330 transferred GBP 6.2m of net claims into the 2019 year, and LPT activity (including a QBE LPT which strengthened the reserve position by GBP 14.8m) altered reserve positions. The combined effect of transaction-driven increases and the modest prior-year release resulted in closing gross claims outstanding of GBP 206.4m at 31 December 2020.
raw_causal_phrases: Within the calendar year net technical result, surpluses of GBP 1.0m on direct business (2019: GBP 0.5m deficit) and GBP 2.5m on reinsurance accepted business (2019: GBP 0.5m deficit) relate to the reassessment of net claims incurred for previous accident years.
Syndicate 3330 2017 YOA was accepted as an RITC as at 1 January 2020 with GBP 6.2m of net claims transferred to Syndicate 1110 2019 YOA.

At 31 December 2020 all Gross Claims Reserves, GBP 59.3m (2019: GBP 74.98m), were covered by the NYMAGIC/Prosight RI arrangements with the whole account stop loss (WASL) attachment point breached in September 2020.

The effective date of the cover is from the 1 January 2020 and this transaction has resulted in an increase to Syndicate 1110's gross written premium of GBP 95.2m and an increase to gross and net technical provisions of GBP 82.2m.
This transaction has strengthened the reserve position of the 2020 year of account by GBP 14.8m.
A provision has been made for unallocated loss adjusted expenses (ULAE) of GBP 5,389k which is included within the technical provisions.
Following novation, the decision was taken to remove loss funds from the paid claims and include the funds within IBNR.

gpt-5-mini.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from balance sheet (explicit). Prior-year development derived from explicit sentence describing surpluses on direct (GBP 1.0m) and reinsurance accepted (GBP 2.5m) business (total release GBP 3.5m). Large transactional items (ADC +GBP 82.2m, RITC +GBP 6.2m, LPTs +/-GBP 14.8m/GBP 58.8m transfers) materially changed gross reserves during 2020; some figures are gross vs net ambiguous in places. 'Direct business' was not broken down by standard Lloyd's LOBs so mapping of the 'direct' release to a single standard LOB is an approximation. Numbers converted from thousands as presented in notes to millions; all monetary values are in the syndicate's functional currency (GBP).
